- Type designations: model 971 with antenna F08, H04, S06, S08, S10, S12, or W06. So type designation: "971". Antennas are model variants. Type designations array: ["971"] — but maybe include antenna variants? The models are 971 with antenna F08, H04, S06, S10, etc. The model family: family name "971" perhaps, models: {"model_id": "971-F08"}, etc. Or model_id "F08", "H04", etc. I'll use model_id like "971 with antenna F08"? Better: models: [{"model_id": "971-F08", "label": "model 971 with antenna F08"}, ...]. Hmm.

The certificate covers a single model 971 with 7 antenna variants. That's >1 model variant, so include model_family with family_name "971" and models list for each antenna.

- Module designation: not applicable (this is not a modular instrument per R85?). Omit or null. The schema says module_designation: "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. Since not mentioned, use null or omit. I'll omit.

- Description: "Automatic level gauge for measuring the level of liquid in fixed storage tanks, model 971 with antenna F08, H04, S06, S08, S10, S12, or W06."

Characteristics: No numeric characteristics given (no accuracy class values, no ranges). Accuracy class 2 goes into recommendation.accuracy_classes.

- id: "R85"
- edition: 1998
- amendment: null (edition 1998 (E) — the (E) is the language of publication, not amendment). Omit amendment.
- scheme: "A"? The scheme of certification — this certificate is issued under... hmm, scheme field in recommendation. The certificate format is a traditional OIML certificate (not MAA). Scheme A is "OIML certificate of conformity" (basic), B is MAA. So scheme "A".
- accuracy_classes: [2] — "for accuracy class 2". Wait, R85 accuracy classes... R85 has accuracy classes... For level gauges, class... anyway, extract "2". Hmm, but accuracy class might be written as "2" — but sometimes "0,2" etc. Text says "for accuracy class 2". So [2].
